transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… thank you. I guess I’m here because something happened while I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt. It’s probably not as bad as I’m making it sound, but I kept getting these really upsetting, unwanted thoughts that I might somehow dishonor her with it—like if I chose the wrong photo placement or the wrong color, it meant I didn’t love her enough.

I know that sounds a little dramatic, maybe, because artists worry about choices all the time, but this felt different. I couldn’t just let it go like normal creative doubt.
Have you noticed these kinds of upsetting, unwanted thoughts happening in other areas of your life, or is this something that only came up while working on the memorial piece?

Mostly it was the memorial piece, I think. That’s the one that really scared me enough to come in. I kept having these awful thoughts that I’d somehow dishonor my aunt if I made the wrong choice—like the photo placement or a color would mean I didn’t love her enough.

I know that probably sounds… overly intense for an art decision. I just couldn’t brush it off the way I usually can with normal creative doubts.
Do you often find yourself worrying about making mistakes or feeling intense pressure to get things exactly right, even outside of your art or memorial work?

I mean… I do care about getting things right, probably more than I should, but the part that really brought me in was with my aunt’s memorial piece. It wasn’t just normal “artist perfectionism,” I don’t think.

I kept having these awful thoughts that if I put a photo in the wrong place, or chose the wrong color, it somehow meant I was dishonoring her—or that I didn’t love her enough. And I knew that sounded unreasonable, but I couldn’t just brush it off like I usually can with regular creative doubts. Does that make sense?
Have you had any other intrusive or upsetting thoughts recently that aren’t related to the memorial piece—thoughts that come into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

Not really… or at least, I haven’t noticed anything that feels as intense outside of that. The main thing was when I was working on my aunt’s memorial piece.

I kept getting these awful thoughts that I might dishonor her somehow, just by making the wrong choice—like where I put a photo, or what color I used—and then it would feel like that meant I didn’t love her enough. I know that probably sounds a bit much, but it felt really upsetting, and I couldn’t just shake it off like normal creative doubt.

When you had those upsetting thoughts about the memorial piece, did you feel driven to do something—like checking, redoing parts, or other actions—to try to reduce the distress or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say it was anything dramatic, but I did keep sort of… going back to things.

Like I’d reread the label text again and again, or nudge the same objects on the table just a little, and then check the layout photos over and over until it felt “settled,” I guess. Part of me knew it was already fine, which makes it feel a bit embarrassing to say, but I’d lose studio time because I couldn’t quite leave it alone. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

When you were going back to check or adjust things with the memorial piece, was it because you felt a strong need to prevent something specific from happening—like feeling certain that if you didn’t, you would be dishonoring your aunt?

I think… yes, kind of. I don’t know if I fully believed something specific would happen, exactly, but it felt like I couldn’t risk leaving it wrong.

So I’d end up rereading the label text, nudging the same objects on the table, checking the layout photos over and over until it felt… settled. Even though another part of me knew it was probably already fine. It’s a little embarrassing, because it wasn’t productive anymore—I was just losing studio time. Does that answer what you mean?
Have these kinds of thoughts or behaviors—like the need to check or redo things—ever significantly interfered with your work, relationships, or daily life outside of this memorial piece?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m still getting most of my work done, so I don’t want to make it sound like everything is falling apart or anything.

But the extra time I lose in the studio has started to matter. I missed a grant deadline because I kept getting stuck checking and reworking things, and I also backed out of a gallery talk I’d actually wanted to do. I feel kind of embarrassed saying that, because it sounds avoidable, but… yeah, it has interfered some.
How long have these thoughts and checking behaviors been going on?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I didn’t really mark when it started, because at first it just felt like me being careful with the work.

It’s been long enough that I’ve noticed the pattern, though… not just a one-day thing. I’m sorry, I know that’s not very precise. Do you mean like when I first noticed it, or when it started actually taking up time?
Can you estimate how long these thoughts and checking behaviors have been going on, even if it started subtly?

I wish I had a cleaner answer. I really don’t know exactly how long.

It wasn’t like one week it suddenly started, or at least I didn’t notice it that way. At first it just seemed like being careful, and then at some point I realized I was going back over the same things more than I needed to. So… I can say it’s been long enough to become a pattern, but I’m honestly not sure how to put a number on it.

Is that too vague?
Would you say these thoughts and checking behaviors have been happening for at least several weeks, even if they started off subtly?

I think… probably, yes? Several weeks sounds fair, I just don’t want to overstate it if that makes sense.

It’s definitely not just been a couple of days. I’ve noticed it enough times that it feels like a pattern. I’m sorry, I know that’s still a little imprecise, but “at least several weeks” seems reasonable.
